project.name: dotclaude-hooks-lint
project.description: Lint/lockfile home for the ~/.claude hook scripts — a "thin harness, fat skills" configuration for Claude Code pairing a lightweight AI coding agent with a large library of structured skills, enforcement hooks, and a self-learning memory layer (OpenWolf).

nodes.name: post-read.js
nodes.summary: PostToolUse hook for Read that records how many tokens the just-read file cost, updating (or creating) the session's files_read entry so OpenWolf can flag repeated reads and compute token savings.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses the Read tool's stdin payload, skips .wolf/-internal files, estimates token cost of the read content (falling back to the anatomy.md estimate), and persists the result into the session state file.

nodes.name: post-write.js
nodes.summary: PostToolUse hook for Write/Edit that updates anatomy.md with a description and token estimate for the changed file, appends a summarized entry to memory.md, and auto-detects likely bug fixes to propose buglog.json entries.
nodes.languageNotes: detectFixPattern uses a long chain of heuristic regex/diff checks (null-guard additions, early returns, condition changes, import changes, CSS property changes) to classify an edit as a likely bug fix without any AST parsing.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that reads the Write/Edit tool payload, skips .wolf/ and .env files, updates anatomy.md sections/metadata, appends a memory.md summary line, updates session state, and triggers bug-fix auto-detection.

nodes.name: summarizeEdit
nodes.summary: Produces a short human-readable description of an old_string/new_string diff (import changes, function signature changes, condition changes, call/prop additions) for the memory.md log line.

nodes.name: extractCalls
nodes.summary: Extracts probable function-call names from a code snippet via regex, filtering out language keywords.

nodes.name: autoDetectBugFix
nodes.summary: Runs detectFixPattern on an edit and, if it looks like a bug fix not already logged, appends a new synthetic entry to buglog.json (deduping against recent similar entries).

nodes.name: detectFixPattern
nodes.summary: Classifies an old_string/new_string edit against a battery of heuristic patterns (null/undefined guards, early returns, condition tightening, import fixes, return-value changes, off-by-one adjustments, CSS property fixes) to guess whether it represents a bug fix and produce a description.

nodes.name: extractChangedLines
nodes.summary: Computes the set of lines present in new_string but not old_string and returns a truncated preview string.

nodes.name: tokenizeCode
nodes.summary: Splits code into a whitespace/word token array for lightweight similarity comparisons.

nodes.name: findOperatorChange
nodes.summary: Detects common comparison-operator swaps (e.g. == to ===, < to <=) between old and new edit strings.

nodes.name: extractCSSProps
nodes.summary: Parses `property: value` pairs out of a CSS-like code snippet into a Map for before/after comparison.

nodes.name: pre-read.js
nodes.summary: PreToolUse hook for Read that warns via stderr when a file was already read this session (to discourage redundant re-reads) and surfaces the matching anatomy.md description when available.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses the Read tool's stdin payload, skips .wolf/-internal files, checks session state for a prior read of the same file (warning if repeated), looks up anatomy.md for a description, and records the read in session state.

nodes.name: pre-write.js
nodes.summary: PreToolUse hook that cross-references write content against cerebrum.md Do-Not-Repeat patterns and buglog.json known fixes, emitting stderr warnings when a known anti-pattern is about to be committed.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that reads the hook payload and dispatches to checkCerebrum and checkBugLog to validate pending write content against known patterns.

nodes.name: checkCerebrum
nodes.summary: Parses the Do-Not-Repeat section of cerebrum.md, converts each entry into a regex pattern (with wildcard support), and warns to stderr if the pending write content matches any pattern.

nodes.name: checkBugLog
nodes.summary: Tokenizes pending write content and compares against buglog.json entries filtered by file and tag overlap, warning to stderr when the edit appears to re-introduce a known bug.

nodes.name: tokenize
nodes.summary: Lowercases and splits text into a stop-word-filtered token set used for buglog relevance matching.

nodes.name: session-start.js
nodes.summary: SessionStart hook that cleans up stale .tmp files, initializes fresh per-session state, appends a new session header to memory.md, reminds Claude if cerebrum.md/buglog.json are stale or empty, and increments the lifetime session counter in token-ledger.json.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Cleans stale .tmp files, creates a fresh session state file, appends a session header table to memory.md, checks cerebrum.md freshness/entry count and buglog.json emptiness (warning via stderr), and bumps total_sessions in token-ledger.json.

nodes.name: shared.js
nodes.summary: Shared utility module for all OpenWolf lifecycle hooks: atomic JSON read/write, markdown read/append, anatomy.md parsing/serialization, description extraction, token estimation, timestamp formatting, stdin reading, and path normalization.
nodes.languageNotes: writeJSON implements an atomic-write pattern (write to a randomized .tmp file, then rename) with a Windows-specific fallback for when rename fails due to a held file handle.

nodes.name: getWolfDir
nodes.summary: Resolves the project's .wolf/ directory path, preferring CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR over cwd so hooks work regardless of session working directory.

nodes.name: getSessionFilePath
nodes.summary: Builds the path to the per-session state JSON file, sanitizing the session ID against a safe-character regex to prevent path traversal.

nodes.name: ensureWolfDir
nodes.summary: Exits the hook process silently if the .wolf/ directory doesn't exist, so hooks no-op gracefully in non-OpenWolf projects.

nodes.name: readJSON
nodes.summary: Reads and parses a JSON file, returning a caller-supplied fallback value on any error.

nodes.name: writeJSON
nodes.summary: Writes JSON data atomically via a randomized temp file plus rename, with a direct-write fallback for platforms (Windows) where rename can fail.

nodes.name: readMarkdown
nodes.summary: Reads a markdown file's contents, returning an empty string on failure.

nodes.name: appendMarkdown
nodes.summary: Appends a line to a markdown file, creating its parent directory if needed.

nodes.name: parseAnatomy
nodes.summary: Parses anatomy.md's markdown structure into a Map of section keys to file entries (filename, description, token estimate) for lookup by the read/write hooks.

nodes.name: serializeAnatomy
nodes.summary: Serializes the in-memory anatomy sections map plus metadata back into anatomy.md's markdown format.

nodes.name: extractDescription
nodes.summary: Derives a short human-readable description of a file for anatomy.md by inspecting its extension, path conventions, and content (doc comments, exports, config keys) via an extensive per-language/per-filetype heuristic dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: A large single function with dozens of branches covering many file types and naming conventions (hooks, configs, tests, docs, etc.) rather than a table-driven dispatch — a prime bloat-audit candidate given its size relative to the rest of the module.

nodes.name: estimateTokens
nodes.summary: Estimates token count for a piece of text/code using a simple character-per-token heuristic differentiated by content type.

nodes.name: timestamp
nodes.summary: Returns the current time as an ISO 8601 string.

nodes.name: timeShort
nodes.summary: Returns the current time formatted as a short HH:MM string for memory.md log lines.

nodes.name: readStdin
nodes.summary: Asynchronously collects and returns all data piped to the hook process's stdin, used to receive the Claude Code hook JSON payload.

nodes.name: normalizePath
nodes.summary: Normalizes a filesystem path to forward slashes for consistent cross-platform comparison.

nodes.name: stop.js
nodes.summary: Stop hook that finalizes a session: builds a token-ledger.json session entry from accumulated read/write stats, warns if heavily-edited files lack a buglog entry or cerebrum.md is stale, and appends a session summary line to memory.md.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Entry point that loads session state, short-circuits if there was no activity, runs the missing-buglog and cerebrum-freshness checks, computes token totals, records a new session entry in token-ledger.json, and appends a memory.md summary line.

nodes.name: checkForMissingBugLogs
nodes.summary: Warns via stderr if any file was edited 3+ times this session but buglog.json was never written to, prompting Claude to log any fixes.

nodes.name: checkCerebrumFreshness
nodes.summary: Warns via stderr if cerebrum.md hasn't been modified in over 24 hours despite 3+ files being written this session.

nodes.name: hooks-cursor.json

nodes.name: run-hook.cmd
nodes.summary: Cross-platform polyglot wrapper script that dispatches named hook scripts to bash — on Windows it locates Git Bash (standard install paths or PATH) via the batch portion, and on Unix the same file is interpreted directly as a shell script that execs the target hook with 'bash'.
nodes.languageNotes: Polyglot file: the leading `: << 'CMDBLOCK' ... CMDBLOCK` fence is a bash here-doc no-op that hides the entire Windows batch section from bash, while cmd.exe only ever sees up to the CMDBLOCK marker. Hook scripts are intentionally named without a .sh extension so Claude Code's Windows auto-detection doesn't mishandle them.

nodes.name: bump-version.sh
nodes.summary: CLI tool that bumps version numbers across all files declared in .version-bump.json, with a --check mode to detect version drift and an --audit mode that greps the repo for stale version strings the config missed.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses jq to read/write dotted JSON field paths (e.g. plugins.0.version), converting dot-notation to jq's bracket syntax via sed before querying or mutating the config file in place.

nodes.name: read_json_field
nodes.summary: Reads a dotted field path (e.g. plugins.0.version) from a JSON file by converting it to a jq path expression.

nodes.name: write_json_field
nodes.summary: Writes a value to a dotted field path in a JSON file in place, preserving the rest of the file's formatting via a temp-file swap.

nodes.name: cmd_check
nodes.summary: Reports the current version recorded in each declared file and flags drift when they disagree.

nodes.name: cmd_audit
nodes.summary: Runs cmd_check then greps the repository for old version strings not covered by the declared file list, using configured exclude patterns.

nodes.name: cmd_bump
nodes.summary: Writes a new version string into every declared file's configured field.

nodes.name: lint-shell.sh
nodes.summary: Lints shell scripts in the repository by running ShellCheck and syntax checks, with modes to target only changed files, the full tracked baseline (--all), or an explicit file list, and an optional --format pass through shfmt.
nodes.languageNotes: Detects shell scripts both by .sh extension and by inspecting the shebang line for bash/dash/ksh/sh interpreters, so extensionless executable scripts are still caught.

nodes.name: is_shell_file
nodes.summary: Determines whether a given path is a shell script by checking its extension or shebang line.

nodes.name: add_shell_file
nodes.summary: Adds a candidate path to the working set of shell files to lint, validating it is a real shell script first.

nodes.name: collect_all_shell_files
nodes.summary: Collects every tracked shell script in the repository for the --all lint mode.

nodes.name: collect_changed_shell_files
nodes.summary: Collects shell scripts that have been changed relative to git, the default lint scope when no flags or files are given.

nodes.name: collect_requested_shell_files
nodes.summary: Collects shell scripts from an explicit list of paths passed as command-line arguments.

nodes.name: syntax_shell_for
nodes.summary: Determines which shell interpreter (bash/dash/ksh/sh) to use for a syntax check based on the script's shebang.

nodes.name: run_syntax_checks
nodes.summary: Runs shell syntax validation (e.g. bash -n) across the collected set of shell files and reports failures.

nodes.name: sync-to-codex-plugin.sh
nodes.summary: Syncs the tracked plugin content of this superpowers checkout into the prime-radiant-inc/openai-codex-plugins fork: clones the fork fresh, rsyncs upstream plugin files while excluding infra/docs/scripts not meant for Codex distribution, preserves OpenAI-owned marketplace metadata, then commits, pushes a sync branch, and opens a PR. Supports dry-run, auto-confirm, an existing local checkout, a configurable base branch, and a bootstrap mode for first-time plugin creation.
nodes.languageNotes: Anchors exclude patterns with a leading '/' to avoid accidentally matching nested directories of the same name (e.g. skills/brainstorming/scripts/ vs top-level /scripts/), and is designed to be deterministic so re-running against the same upstream SHA reproduces an identical diff.

nodes.name: path_has_directory_exclude
nodes.summary: Checks whether a path falls under one of the configured directory exclude patterns, anchored to avoid matching nested directories of the same name.

nodes.name: append_git_ignored_directory_excludes
nodes.summary: Extends the exclude list with directories that are git-ignored in the upstream checkout, so untracked build artifacts are not synced.

nodes.name: append_git_ignored_file_excludes
nodes.summary: Extends the exclude list with individual git-ignored files so they are not copied into the destination plugin.

nodes.name: overlay_destination_paths
nodes.summary: Computes the set of destination-owned paths (OpenAI marketplace metadata) that must be preserved rather than overwritten by the sync.

nodes.name: copy_local_destination_overlay
nodes.summary: Copies the preserved destination-owned files back into the fresh clone after the rsync overwrite step.

nodes.name: prepare_preview_checkout
nodes.summary: Sets up a temporary checkout of the fork used to preview the diff before applying and pushing changes.

nodes.name: prepare_apply_checkout
nodes.summary: Sets up the checkout used for the real (non-dry-run) apply-and-push sync.

nodes.name: apply_to_preview_checkout
nodes.summary: Applies the rsync content changes to the preview checkout so a diff can be shown before committing for real.

nodes.name: copy_preserved_destination_metadata
nodes.summary: Copies OpenAI-owned marketplace metadata files from the destination back into place after the sync overwrite so they are not clobbered by upstream content.

nodes.name: prepare_sync_source
nodes.summary: Prepares the upstream source directory (fresh clone or --local checkout) that will be rsynced into the destination plugin.

nodes.name: SKILL.md

nodes.languageNotes: Structured as a behavior-shaping skill prompt (SKILL.md convention) rather than reference documentation — written as directives for an AI agent to follow, with an explicit anti-pattern warning and a hard checklist.

nodes.name: spec-document-reviewer-prompt.md

nodes.name: frame-template.html

nodes.languageNotes: Pure static HTML/CSS with placeholder comments (<!-- BRANDING -->, <!-- CONTENT -->) marking injection points for server-side content substitution; no JavaScript or dynamic logic of its own.

nodes.name: start-server.sh
nodes.summary: Launches the brainstorming skill's local companion web server (server.cjs), creating a per-session state directory, generating a random server-instance id, choosing foreground vs. background execution based on environment (Codex CI, Windows/Git Bash), and printing a JSON connection payload once the server reports it has started.
nodes.languageNotes: Bash script with careful cross-platform handling: detects MSYS/Cygwin/MinGW shells to force foreground mode (since Windows reaps detached background processes and cannot verify POSIX PIDs), uses umask 077 and chmod 600 to keep session secrets owner-only, and resolves the owning harness PID via the parent's PPID for a later liveness watchdog.

nodes.name: stop-server.sh
nodes.summary: Stops a running brainstorming companion server given its session directory, verifying the PID actually belongs to this session's server instance (via a per-start server id embedded in the process command line) before signaling it, escalating from SIGTERM to SIGKILL, and cleaning up ephemeral /tmp session directories while preserving persistent project-scoped ones.
nodes.languageNotes: Defends against stale/reused PIDs after reboot or PID wraparound by matching a random per-start server-instance-id against the target process's command-line arguments (via /proc/<pid>/cmdline or ps) before sending any signal — fails closed as 'stale_pid' on any ambiguity.

nodes.name: is_windows_like_shell
nodes.summary: Detects whether the script is running under a Windows-like shell (MSYS, Cygwin, MinGW) by checking OSTYPE, MSYSTEM, and uname -s, used to decide whether the server must run in foreground mode.

nodes.name: command_has_server_id
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given PID's command-line arguments contain the expected --brainstorm-server-id=<id> flag, used to confirm a PID truly belongs to this session's server before signaling it.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: This repo is ~/.claude: a "thin harness, fat skills" configuration for Claude Code. The README frames the philosophy in one line — the agent itself stays lightweight, while a large library of structured skills, enforcement hooks, and a self-learning memory layer (OpenWolf) carry the real complexity. Everything else in this tour fills in the pieces this sentence gestures at.

tour.title: The Conceptual Entry Point: CLAUDE.md
tour.description: There is no compiled binary or server process to boot here, so CLAUDE.md plays the role a main.ts or app.py would in a typical project — it is the first file Claude Code reads every session, and it drives everything downstream. It defines the skill-invocation routing table (which skill to call for which situation), a project-tier rigor ladder, and an accumulated changelog of infrastructure gotchas learned the hard way. Treat this as the map for the rest of the tour: nearly every subsystem you'll see next is referenced from here.

tour.title: Wiring the Harness: settings.json
tour.description: CLAUDE.md describes policy in prose; settings.json is where that policy becomes mechanism. The user-level settings.json wires environment variables, tool permissions, model selection, the full hooks pipeline, and enabled plugins, while the project-local .claude/settings.json wires OpenWolf's lifecycle hooks (SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop) to concrete scripts under .wolf/hooks/. Two files, two scopes — one global to the user, one scoped to this repo.

tour.title: Root Lifecycle Hooks & Enforcement Gates
tour.description: CLAUDE.md's routing table (Step 2) says "grilling must run before writing-plans" — but prose alone doesn't stop anyone from skipping it. These four hooks are the real enforcement: pre-skill-gate.js blocks the writing-plans skill unless grilling already ran this session, and post-skill-record.js is what lets it know — it writes a marker file every time a skill executes. The cerebrum-write-guard pair does the same pattern for a different problem: the PostToolUse half records cerebrum.md's mtime after a write, and the PreToolUse half compares against that baseline to catch a concurrent session clobbering the same file.
tour.languageLesson: This is a classic pre/post hook pairing: one hook stamps state at the end of an action, and a second hook checks that state before allowing a later action. It's a lightweight alternative to a database lock — a JSON marker file on disk plays the same role.

tour.title: OpenWolf's Shared Hook Utilities
tour.description: Every OpenWolf lifecycle hook — session-start, stop, pre/post read and write — needs the same primitives: atomic JSON read/write, markdown append, token estimation, path normalization. shared.js is the single module all of them import, which is why it has the highest fan-in of any file in this codebase. session-start.js and stop.js show what gets built on top of it: session-start initializes fresh per-session state and warns if cerebrum.md is stale, while stop.js finalizes the session, builds a token-ledger entry, and appends a summary line to memory.md.

tour.title: The Living Memory Files
tour.description: The hooks from Step 5 don't just track state internally — they read and write plain markdown files that are meant to be read by both Claude and the human. cerebrum.md holds durable, curated learnings (rewritten wholesale by a weekly reflection cron), while memory.md is an append-only per-session log of what changed. The rule file documents the protocol binding them together: check anatomy and cerebrum before generating code, cross-reference the buglog, update memory after edits.

tour.title: Exposing Memory via MCP: openwolf-api
tour.description: The memory files from Step 6 are useful to Claude directly, but openwolf-api makes them queryable as a proper service — a FastAPI application mounted as an MCP server that exposes read-only endpoints over a project's bug log, memory log, cerebrum learnings, and anatomy map. This is the bridge between the file-based memory layer and the MCP tool-calling surface every Claude Code session can reach through .mcp.json's registration.
tour.languageLesson: fastapi-mcp wraps a normal FastAPI app so its existing REST endpoints are automatically exposed as MCP tools too — one implementation, two calling conventions (HTTP and MCP).

tour.title: Process Skills: Brainstorm to Ship
tour.description: CLAUDE.md's routing table names a sequence — brainstorming, then grilling, then writing-plans — before any code gets touched. These SKILL.md files are the actual instruction sets Claude follows for two of the heaviest steps in that pipeline. brainstorming/SKILL.md defines the checklist for turning an idea into a validated spec with a self-review and user-approval gate; writing-skills/SKILL.md defines a TDD-adapted methodology for authoring new skills, applied recursively to the skill library itself.

tour.title: Testing & Multi-Platform Distribution
tour.description: The Superpowers skill library isn't Claude Code-only — it's designed to run across multiple agent harnesses. hooks.json wires SessionStart for Claude Code, while hooks-codex.json wires the equivalent event for Codex with its own variable convention (${PLUGIN_ROOT} instead of ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}); porting-to-a-new-harness.md documents the three invariant components that make this portability possible. run-skill-tests.sh is how the library verifies its own skills actually work, invoking the Claude Code CLI to execute fast unit tests by default and slower integration tests on demand.

tour.title: Top-Level Skills & Infra Reference
tour.description: Alongside the vendored Superpowers library, this repo has its own top-level skills/ directory of project-specific skills. senior-engineering-partner/SKILL.md is the deepest of these — a full pair-programming and code-review persona with mode triggers, a security floor, and a phase-aware rigor ladder. claude-infra-reference/SKILL.md is the connective tissue: it documents conventions (custom agent registration, brand/document skill rules, browser-automation tool choice) that other skills point to instead of repeating.

tour.title: A Real Subsystem: the LangSmith Plugin
tour.description: Everything so far has been harness configuration and process skills. langsmith-plugin is an actual shipped TypeScript application living inside this repo — it traces Claude Code sessions to LangSmith for observability. index.ts is its public barrel, re-exporting the programmatic API; state.ts is the module every hook depends on (highest fan-in in the whole plugin), providing file-backed session state with optimistic locking for concurrent-hook safety; stop.ts is where it all comes together, tracing the completed session's transcript to LangSmith and pruning old state.
tour.languageLesson: Optimistic file locking (read, compute, write-if-unchanged, retry on conflict) is a lightweight alternative to a real lock file when multiple hook processes might touch the same state concurrently — no external coordination service required.

tour.title: Build & CI: From TypeScript to Shipped Bundle
tour.description: The source in Step 11 has to become something Claude Code can actually execute as a hook — a plain Node.js script, not a TypeScript module. esbuild.config.mjs compiles all 9 hook entry points into standalone ESM bundles, injecting the package version as a compile-time constant. ci.yml is the safety net: it runs on every push and PR, installs dependencies, runs tests, builds, and — critically — verifies the committed bundle/ directory actually matches what the build produces, so a stale bundle can never ship silently.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions CI here does double duty: it's both a test runner and a drift detector, failing the build if generated output (bundle/) doesn't match source — the same discipline a linter applies to formatting, applied to build artifacts.

tour.title: Publishing the Docs Site
tour.description: With dozens of skills spread across skills/ and superpowers/skills/, discoverability becomes its own problem — pull-skills.mjs solves it by walking every SKILL.md, parsing its frontmatter, rewriting internal links, and generating a static docs-site page for each one. The README documents the sync script's idempotency guarantees, so re-running it never produces spurious diffs. This is the last mile connecting the skill library from Steps 8-10 to the publicly browsable architecture explainer the top-level README (Step 1) links out to.

tour.title: Enforcement Capstone: Lint & Secret Scanning
tour.description: Closing the loop back to CLAUDE.md's security posture: eslint.config.js scopes eslint-plugin-security rules specifically to the hooks you saw in Steps 4-5, hard-banning eval and child_process misuse and warning on non-literal filesystem paths — because a hook runs on every session, a vulnerability there is a vulnerability in the harness itself. .gitleaks.toml is the complementary secret-scanning gate, extending the default ruleset while allowlisting vendored third-party directories like superpowers/ that this repo doesn't own and can't audit line-by-line. Together they're the automated counterpart to CLAUDE.md's security-floor rule, enforced pre-commit rather than just documented.
